title: Evidence-gated induction of reusable research-agent skills
research_question: Can a small deterministic pipeline block unverified self-improvement while preserving enough provenance for a human to audit promotion?

claim.statement: The pipeline blocks success traces and activatable skills unless structural validation, evidence integrity, a bound semantic verification receipt, explicit human acceptance, and ready lifecycle status all pass.
claim.measurable_target: Every promoted trace has nine passing gates, content-addressed evidence, a replayed semantic receipt, and bound human acceptance.
kill_conditions: A success trace or activatable skill is emitted without a bound verification receipt.
A success trace or activatable skill is emitted without explicit human acceptance.
A parked candidate is promoted or emits a success trace or activatable skill.

assumptions.statement: Candidates arrive as structured JSON rather than arbitrary prose.
assumptions.cost: A separate ingestion layer is needed for free-form research notes.
assumptions.weakening: Add a schema-producing parser whose output still passes the same gates.

assumptions.statement: Public demo evidence is represented by repository-local artifacts.
assumptions.cost: The demo does not fetch or authenticate remote literature sources.
assumptions.weakening: Introduce signed remote evidence adapters without changing packet semantics.

proof_route: Validate the candidate against a versioned machine-readable schema.
Resolve evidence inside the repository and bind each file by SHA-256.
Evaluate assumption, comparison, falsifiability, and induction structural gates.
Replay a registered executable verifier and bind its receipt to the semantic subject.
Require an explicit human acceptance record bound to that exact receipt.
Emit a decision packet before creating any success trace.
Create a trace and reusable skill only for an all-pass decision.

novelty.contribution: A compact executable illustration of evidence-gated external agent evolution.
novelty.collision_status: No field-level novelty claim is made.
novelty.coverage: Comparison is limited to two common workflow alternatives; it is not a literature review.

comparators.name: Free-form reflection log
comparators.difference: Retains narrative lessons without a typed decision packet or promotion gate.
comparators.tradeoff: Simpler to write, but harder to validate or replay automatically.

comparators.name: Ungated trace retention
comparators.difference: Stores every attempted workflow as reusable memory regardless of verifier status.
comparators.tradeoff: Collects more traces, but can turn failed self-output into future policy.

expected_value.story: Show the smallest auditable path from a candidate proposal to a provenance-linked skill.
expected_value.success_metric: A clean Python environment reproduces byte-identical artifacts across runs.

evidence.summary: The public candidate contract used before any promotion decision.
Determinism and negative-path tests for the candidate-to-skill pipeline.
One-command entry points for the demo, tests, and public-release audit.

risks: Structural gates cannot establish that a scientific theorem is true.
Repository-local evidence can be incomplete even when all referenced files exist.
A fixed policy may need domain-specific verifiers for real research decisions.
limitations: This public demo is deterministic and offline; it is not a production multi-agent runtime.
The comparison gate checks declared scope, not exhaustive scholarly novelty.
Human reviewers remain responsible for scientific and deployment decisions.
reward_questions: Are these gates sufficient to justify retaining this workflow as a reusable skill?
Which additional domain verifier would be required before using the pattern on a theorem claim?

skill_blueprint.name: evidence-gated-skill-induction
skill_blueprint.description: Promote a successful research workflow into a reusable skill only after explicit evidence and policy gates pass.
skill_blueprint.trigger: A research-agent workflow appears reusable and is being considered for persistent memory.
workflow: Validate the candidate against the declared schema.
Resolve and hash every evidence locator without leaving the repository.
Classify assumptions and record their costs and weakening routes.
Check comparison scope, measurable target, kill conditions, risks, and limitations.
Replay the registered verifier and bind its result to the complete semantic subject.
Write a decision packet before assigning a success signal.
Require explicit human acceptance bound to the same receipt.
Induce the reusable skill only when every required gate passes.
outputs: Verified success trace only after receipt replay and human acceptance
Activation-eligible reusable skill only after receipt replay and human acceptance
validation: Structural, evidence-integrity, semantic-verification, and human-acceptance states remain distinct.
Every evidence artifact has a repository-relative locator and SHA-256 digest.
The success trace binds the exact decision packet, verification receipt, and human acceptance record.
A failed gate prevents both success trace and skill emission.
failure_modes: Treating schema validity as evidence that the scientific claim is correct.
Assigning reward from model confidence without a verifier or human signal.
Losing the linkage between evidence, decision packet, trace, and induced skill.
